gate.PASS: mechanism clears AND levels >= GG8 + 5 AND levels >= 47.
gate.REJECT: levels <= 30, or the inert condition above.
gate.UNDECIDED_BY_BENCH: everything else. The 12.5-level MDE cannot resolve this arm on levels alone.

mechanism_is_the_verdict.inert_if: build_model fires in <= 2 of 25, in which case REJECT regardless of levels
mechanism_is_the_verdict.predict_defined_by_the_builder: >= 12 of 25 games, against the actor's measured 5 of 25

gate.read_against: GG8 from the same wave, NEVER against ONEWAVE

GG10.independent_variable: THE DELEGATED BUILDER, and nothing else, READ AGAINST GG8 AND NEVER AGAINST ONEWAVE. GG10 is byte-identical to GG8 plus apply_orchestrator: a build_model tool that hands the last 4 within-level transitions to a separate builder generation whose only job is to write predict(). GG8 asks the acting model to write its own world model between moves; GG10 asks a second generation to write it.

gate.PASS: mechanism gate clears AND levels >= 47. Ships to the next slot per rule 15(a).
gate.REJECT: levels <= 30, which is 2.4 sd below the family mean. Rule 15(c) bars it permanently.
gate.UNDECIDED_BY_BENCH: 31 to 46 levels. Report the mechanism counters, ship nothing, keep ONEWAVE.
gate.note: the measured Flash-Next MDE at n=1 vs n=1 is 12.5 levels, so levels alone cannot resolve this arm.
gate.on_mechanism_failure: the level total is NOT read as a verdict; the arm did not run.

GG8.independent_variable: THE CERTIFICATION PREDICATE, and nothing else. validate(predict) stops being whole-board exact equality over 4,096 cells and becomes a LOCAL predicate: predict may return '?' for any cell it does not claim, unclaimed cells are skipped in the diff, coverage is reported, and a board claiming nothing is bucketed rather than passed. The transition log is level-filtered so cross-level pairs never enter it. Model, sampling, clock, concurrency, schedule and game set are all held at ONEWAVE.

blocking_fix_applied_first.why: The guard was stale, not the prompt. Its own comment records the cap being moved 2,000 -> 3,200 when the worked example was added; the abstaining-render overlay then added the '?' cell convention and the coverage floor, taking the addendum to 3,540 chars. That is ~1,200 tokens, 2.5% of the 48,128-token history budget. Shrinking the prompt instead would have deleted the worked example, which IS the arm: arm V measured predict() written in 1 of 25 games without it.

control: ONEWAVE, 46 levels. Flash-Next family 44 / 40 / 47 / 41 / 46, mean 43.6, sd 3.16, MDE 12.5 at n=1 vs n=1.
tonights_slot: ONEWAVE, unchanged, and by arithmetic rather than by default. Pooled within-config sd is 0.542; against our banked 4.61, P(a single draw sets a new max) is 17.1% for ONEWAVE (mean 4.095), 5.4% for S-wavefit (3.738), 1.9% for G-flashnext48k (3.487). Swapping would lower tonight's expected draw. If either arm clears its mechanism gate AND lands >= 47 levels by 15:00 PDT it ships tonight per rule 15(a); otherwise the winner carries tomorrow.
what_this_cannot_show: Neither arm is worth the 12.5-level MDE, so the modal outcome for both is UNDECIDED-BY-BENCH and neither can be shown to close any part of the 4.61 vs 12.88 gap. The mechanism counters are the deliverable: this is the first clean read on whether the certify-then-plan architecture every published high scorer uses is reachable on open weights.
why_two_arms_at_once: GG10 is byte-identical to GG8 plus apply_orchestrator, so the two runs plus the shipping ONEWAVE bench form a ladder, 46 / GG8 / GG10, in which GG10 minus GG8 is a clean single-variable read on the delegated builder. Running either alone costs the same wall clock and throws that contrast away. Max 2 concurrent GPU sessions, so this is the whole wave.
